messages:
Liza (Support): @Jin thanks for sending examples — filing this here so eng/ML can triage. Customer (Acme) says after the azalea model bump yesterday their responses are noticeably shorter and less friendly in tone, which is impacting UX. They attached a pair of outputs for the same prompt.

Jin (Acme Customer): repro attached — 2 requests, id=rc-9182 and rc-9183. Both same prompt. Previously on azalea-2.1 we got 4–5 sentences with a brief acknowledgement. On azalea-2.2 answers are one-liners, no closing or clarifying question. Not huge semantic regressions, more of a stylistic/conversational regression.

Liza (Support): Copied sample from customer (sanitized):

Prompt:
"""
We need to summarize this meeting transcript and list action items, and include 2 suggested follow-ups to clarify scope.
"""

Response from azalea-2.1 (old):
"""
Summary: The team agreed to prioritize the payments API refactor, with Alice owning API changes and Raj handling DB migration. Action items: 1) Draft migration plan (Alice) 2) Run load tests (Raj) 3) Update docs (Ivy). Suggested follow-ups: 1) Can you confirm the rollback window for the DB migration? 2) Do we need a support runbook for the first 48 hours after rollout?
Thanks — let me know if you want the items formatted as a Trello/Asana task list.
"""

Response from azalea-2.2 (new):
"""
Summary: Team will refactor payments API. Action items: 1) Draft migration plan 2) Run load tests 3) Update docs.
"""

Liza (Support): Customer says the removal of the follow-ups/soft closing is causing friction with their product which relies on the model to propose clarifying questions. They flagged it as regression after our model rollout at 02:00 UTC.

Noah (Product): @Maria any known config or system prompt changes during the rollout? Did we modify the default system instruction or any safety/conciseness tuning?

Maria (ML Eng): Not intentionally. Rollout notes: azalea-2.2 pushed regionally (us-west) at 01:45 UTC, global at ~02:05 UTC. The model checkpoint includes a small RLHF tuning pass to reduce verbosity for short prompts — intended to cut token usage for microcalls. We have telemetry that shows avg response length dropped ~18% overall in the canary.

Eli (SRE): Logs for the two request ids Jin gave: rc-9182 -> routed to azalea-2.1 (before global), rc-9183 -> azalea-2.2. I pulled the raw API payloads and they are identical aside from model param.

ops-bot: Deploy event: azalea-2.2 promoted to stable at 02:03 UTC by rollout-bot.

Liza (Support): Repro steps we ran locally (matching customer):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"azalea-2.1","input":"[meeting transcript]...","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.2}'
```
Compare by changing model to azalea-2.2. Output diff attached in thread (see sample above).

Maria (ML Eng): Confirmed: the RLHF pass included a conciseness objective for prompts under ~300 tokens. That explains the shorter outputs. It reduced tokens but unintentionally removed auxiliary suggestions/closing phrasings.

Noah (Product): That is unfortunate — product impact > cost savings in this use case. What's the quick mitigation for affected customers? Pin to previous model? Add a system prompt to encourage follow-ups?

Maria (ML Eng): Short-term options: 1) Route this customer's traffic to azalea-2.1-stable (we can pin via tenant routing) — immediate fix. 2) Add a default system instruction in response pipeline for azalea-2.2 for customers who opt-in: e.g., "Include 1–2 clarifying questions and a brief closing sentence." 3) Roll back the conciseness tuning in azalea-2.2 and push a corrected weight (requires a small retrain, 24–48h).

Eli (SRE): Re-routing: ops can add a tenant rule to pin Acme to azalea-2.1-stable. I can do that now if Product/Support approve. No infra risk.

Liza (Support): Jin — would pinning to azalea-2.1-stable be acceptable as an interim? We can also offer a prompt template they can add to their calls.

Jin (Acme Customer): Pinning is acceptable short-term. They prefer we avoid them having to manage system prompts. Ideally we want same model (for perf/cost) but with the follow-ups.

Noah (Product): Ok, plan: immediate pin + opt-in system instruction while ML works on a corrective patch. Maria/Eli can you take action items? I'll draft comms for impacted customers and internal release notes.

Maria (ML Eng): Action items assigned: 1) Create azalea-2.2-verbosity-patch branch and run limited retrain with reduced conciseness weight (ETA 36h). 2) Prepare an opt-in system-instruction flag that Support can toggle per-tenant (hotfix path). I'll open a ticket: RWF-7243.

Eli (SRE): I'll pin Acme tenant to azalea-2.1-stable now. Rule id created: tenant-pin-axc-449. I'll monitor request routing for 1 hour and report back.

Liza (Support): I've informed Jin and offered a temporary credit for any UX regressions. Jin replied OK.

Maria (ML Eng): Quick diagnostic note for the team: the conciseness objective adds a reward term R_c = -lambda * length_norm where lambda=0.08 in 2.2. That lambda caused high penalty for polite closers. For the patch we'll reduce lambda->0.03 and retune on a heldout set that includes explicit conversational tasks so we preserve clarifying question behavior.

Noah (Product): Good — please add evaluation tests for: "always propose 1 clarifying question for instruction: 'summarize and propose follow-ups'" We should fail builds if regression seen.

Liza (Support): Follow-ups:
- Eli: confirm tenant pin done + confirm no perf regression (Eli -> done by 1776315900).
- Maria: open RWF-7243 with patch plan and ETA (Maria -> will do).
- Noah: draft customer comms and internal incident note.
- Support: monitor additional reports and collect more sample pairs.

Jin (Acme Customer): Thanks — appreciate quick turnaround. We'll reopen if we see anything else.

ops-bot: Route rule created tenant-pin-axc-449 by Eli at 02:45 UTC.

Liza (Support): Closing loop here for now. Will keep thread updated when RWF-7243 lands and when patch is promoted.

(Reaction summary: :thumbsup: from Jin, :eyes: from Maria, :dubious: from a couple of product folks)
